title: Tower access is deliberately made expensive
observation: The opening sequence shows sandbags, wire and blocked approaches inside Tower 2. Comms emphasise window cover and friendly access while the builder stays on construction work.
interpretation: This recorded squad invests in layered local denial and a defensible interior rather than spreading everyone immediately into open combat.
response: Inspect alternate entries and roof access before committing to the obvious stairway. Bring demolition and an assigned entry group.
limitation: It is a local fortification plan, not proof the entire tower is impenetrable.

title: Roof awareness and manpower lag behind the walls
observation: Around 29 minutes comms report roughly five to ten roof attackers, request closed doors and ask why only two defenders are present. The POV is inside a heavily restricted tower.
interpretation: A strong interior can still leave the roof and early warning dependent on a small garrison and outside spotters.
response: Coordinate roof pressure with another entry threat; force the defenders to divide attention and report where the FOB actually sits.
limitation: Attacker numbers and the separate main-base loss are comms reports; no complete roof count is claimed.

title: The build plan is sensitive to supply quality
observation: A requested building-supply delivery around 20 minutes is identified in the French original as a mechanical pallet. Construction and inventory management continue around that exchange.
interpretation: Even when transport arrives, the wrong supply category can interrupt the fortification loop.
response: Pressure builders while they wait for the correct stock. For PHNT, use a named supply type, destination and read-back before lifting the pallet.
limitation: The footage does not isolate the delay in seconds or points lost.

title: They reduce the garrison when the tower is quiet
observation: At 50 minutes the caller offers spare players, asks for two to remain with him and sends the others to help elsewhere; a scout outside is also requested.
interpretation: The defence is not purely static. The team tries to turn a fortified position into a manpower saving once immediate pressure falls.
response: Watch for the release window: renewed pressure may force the reduced garrison to call help back. PHNT can practise the same handover with a clear minimum guard.
limitation: This is the explicit order; the exact number who successfully redeployed is not tracked.

title: Construction can make friendly movement awkward
observation: Around 54 minutes the builder says a ring has no door and describes an exit/re-entry problem; the squad asks for a small door. At 75 minutes, after the order to leave, someone again asks how to get out.
interpretation: Defensive density trades against easy reinforcement, withdrawal and regrouping.
response: Time pressure when their squad must redeploy. In PHNT builds, test both directions of travel and reserve an identifiable exit before sealing the perimeter.
limitation: This is a documented access problem, not a measured guarantee that attackers can trap every defender.

title: They eventually trade the tower for scoring survival
observation: The team releases the tower around 75 minutes, then repeatedly asks players to stay alive, revive and regroup in the large circle. Blue advances from 89 at 75:00 to 99 at 81:00 and wins 100-79-12.
interpretation: The fort is a means to the scoring plan; in the finish, preserved bodies take priority over more construction or chasing kills.
response: Contest the safe regroup area and reinforcement route. Do not keep committing resources to an abandoned tower while their scoring population rebuilds elsewhere.
limitation: The score/result is direct; the share of the win caused by this particular order is not isolated.

title: Red remains an active scoring threat late
observation: Red reaches 51 against Blue 54 at 50:00, then 71 by 70:00. Late anchors show Red control and continued progress while Blue is stalled on 99.
interpretation: GI|I is not eliminated by the tower defence; its scoring pressure makes the late regroup meaningful.
response: Keep a reserve for the next zone transition rather than assigning every player to a tower assault.
limitation: HUD anchors establish progress and sampled control, not the hidden tactical route that produced it.
